topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the scope of the lecture on cancer causes and outlines the key learning objectives.

topics.label: Etiology of cancer: genetic, environmental, and epidemiological factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamental concepts of cancer etiology, contrasting endogenous genetic processes and random mutations with environmental exposures and epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Oncogenic infectious agents and viral carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious pathogens contribute to malignant transformation, using Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and xenobiotic metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation and chemical carcinogens induce DNA damage directly or following host metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, tissue microenvironment, and cellular susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic tumor promotion mechanisms and how cellular context, tissue microenvironment, and developmental timing modulate carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the analytical, epidemiological, and experimental methodologies used to identify and evaluate carcinogenic agents.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and risk-benefit considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with a summary and reflections on balancing carcinogenic risks against everyday benefits.
